survey: An open cream envelope, tilted slightly toward the camera. Back panel and flap: the back panel rises behind the photos, and its top flap stands open, pointing up behind them, so it is attached to the panel farthest from the viewer. Front panel: the panel facing the camera has diagonal fold seams running in from both lower corners, and its top edge dips in a deep V almost to the middle of the envelope. The postage stamp and wavy postmark sit on its lower right. Photos: three white-bordered photos stand upright in the pocket between the panels, fanned a little toward the back right. The front photo is narrower than the envelope and fits inside, and its lower part disappears behind the V edge. Small details: the boat in the photo has a short line running to a buoy, and that line ends at the buoy. The tools found no other thin parts, loose ends or branch points. Nothing floats; the photos stand inside the pocket.

errors.where: Envelope front panel (the side facing the camera, with stamp and postmark)
errors.what: The front panel mixes the two sides of an envelope. Because the flap opens from the far panel, the side we see is the address side, and the stamp and postmark agree with that. On a real envelope that side is one flat sheet with a straight top edge. Here it has the diagonal seams and V-shaped top edge of the back, where the side and bottom flaps are glued. The envelope still holds the photos, but an envelope folded this way could not be made, and the stamp would sit on the back.

fix: Open envelope seen from the front: a flat front panel with a straight top edge carries the stamp and postmark, with no fold seams on the front. The triangular flap is open upward behind the photos, attached to the top edge of the back panel. The photos stick up out of the opening at the top.
